$comment: Fixture set for src/schemas/error_envelope.json — API_CONTRACT §1's always-on error body. The schema closes the eight codes and the per-code `details` requirements (if/then); the two custom rules check what a schema cannot: that the body's own `details.http_status` agrees with §1's code→status table, and that an `ai_unavailable` names a rung of the §105 failure ladder.

cases.name: 01_valid_not_found_carries_resource_and_reason
cases.description: API §1's example body, modelled the way CONTRACT NOTES 9 in src/enums.ts says it must be: `merchant_not_found` is not one of the eight codes, so it rides in `details.resource` + `details.reason` and the code stays `not_found` (404, D5).

error.message: 找不到该商户，或它尚未发布。

cases.name: 02_valid_validation_error_with_field_errors
cases.description: A 422 from either service (§1 `field_errors`): the keys are dotted instance paths, not wire fields, which is why the map is exempt from the snake_case rule and the paths still read as JSON-Pointer-ish locations.

error.message: Some fields need another look before we search.

cases.name: 03_valid_ai_unavailable_names_the_ladder_rung
cases.description: Spec §105 / AGENT §2 rule 4: when the AI path fails the caller must be told which rung to take next, so `details.fallback` is from FALLBACK_KIND and `retryable` says whether staying on the AI path is worth another attempt.

error.message: AI 搜索暂时不可用，已切换到普通搜索。

cases.name: 04_valid_rate_limited_with_retry_after
cases.description: API §1's rate limits: `details.retry_after` mirrors the `Retry-After` header and `remaining` is what the caller has left in the window, so the client's backoff is computed rather than guessed.

error.message: Too many searches in the last minute — give it 12 seconds.

cases.name: 05_invalid_http_status_disagrees_with_code
cases.description: §1 binds each code to exactly one status. A `not_found` body that claims 403 would send the SDK's failure ladder down the authorisation branch for a resource that simply is not there — and D5 says a foreign row answers 404, so the disagreement is how enumeration bugs hide.

cases.name: 06_invalid_ai_unavailable_invents_a_fallback
cases.description: `fallback` is the rung the caller should take, and §105's ladder has three: model_fallback, deterministic_search, human. `llm_retry` is a fourth that no client implements, so the response would tell the caller to do something nobody can do.

error.message: The model is busy; we stopped rather than guess.

cases.name: 07_invalid_ai_unavailable_without_ladder_details
cases.description: The same failure with `fallback`/`retryable` absent: the if/then in error_envelope.json demands the keys (code `required`) and the rule refuses an `ai_unavailable` that leaves the caller to guess which rung to climb (spec §105).

cases.name: 08_valid_resource_code_specialises_the_ladder
cases.description: DECISIONS D27: §1's eight codes are the status ladder, and a code may prefix the resource that failed — this is exactly what the platform sends on a merchant 404, captured live by `scripts/verify_payload_conformance.mjs`. The status comes from the `_not_found` suffix, and `details.resource` is deliberately not required because the code already names the subject.

cases.name: 09_invalid_resource_code_status_disagrees_with_suffix
cases.description: The derivation D27 adds is the check the closed enum could not express at all: a `slot_not_found` served with 403 reads as a missing row to any client that resolves status from the suffix, and D5 makes a foreign row answer 404 for precisely that reason. This case is what keeps `ladderErrorCode` load-bearing rather than decorative.

cases.name: 10_invalid_code_is_neither_ladder_nor_suffix
cases.description: A snake_case string ending in no ladder suffix is not a code: `validation_failed` resembles `validation_error`, would be served 422 by luck, and matches neither branch of the anyOf. If any string passed, §1's table would stop being a contract and become documentation.

cases.name: 11_invalid_extra_top_level_key
cases.description: §1 says the error body is always `{ error: { … } }` — `error` is the only top-level key. A sibling `request_id` (the right value, the wrong place) would be missed by every client that reads `body.error.request_id`, so the correlation id is lost at the log boundary.

error.message: Something broke on our side. The request id above is what to quote.
